A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPDstergm research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original SBM and STERGM simulations and change-point analyses of MIT cellphone interactions and stock-market networks.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulation results and change-point analyses of MIT cellphone interactions and stock-market networks.

M1.justification: The STERGM construction, Group Fused Lasso objective, ADMM updates, Newton-Raphson and Group Lasso procedures, thresholding, and BIC selection are retained. Algorithm 1 is compressed and moved to Appendix D without a documented procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same temporally dependent SBM simulations, STERGM simulations, MIT cellphone data, and DJIA stock-return networks. No dataset, population, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–6 retain gSeg and kerSeg with both network and network-statistic inputs. The corresponding real-data comparisons in Figures 4–5 also retain the same competitors.

E3.justification: Simulation sizes, generating parameters, true change points, evaluation metrics, optimization budgets, tuning grids, and comparator thresholds are unchanged. Stock-network preprocessing is retained. The stopping and post-processing rules move to Appendix D without changing their settings.

E4.justification: The comparisons across temporal dependence, network size, and network-statistic complexity remain unchanged, as do the two real-data case studies. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over ten Monte Carlo trials per simulation specification. There are no new seed disclosures, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical comparisons.

E6.justification: All 90 method-result rows in Tables 1–6 match numerically. Tables 7–8 retain the same detected dates and associated events, and Figures 2–5 retain the same plotted content.

T1.justification: v4 adds Proposition 1 and Appendix A, providing an ADMM residual-convergence proof conditional on exact subproblem minimization. Sections 2.1 and 3.2–3.3 add convexity and positive-definiteness arguments; Propositions 2–3 largely restate existing update derivations. The network-space definition also changes, omitting v3's explicit no-self-loop restriction.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a STERGM-based multiple-change-point estimator using GFL and ADMM, BIC selection, an R package, and effective detection under temporal and dyadic dependence. The explicit 'unsupervised' description and rewritten contribution statements retain this scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds a rationale for choosing Newton-Raphson over gradient descent based on second-order information, convergence, and update stability. It also adds application-based support for separability. Existing empirical interpretations and the limitations concerning valued networks, changing network sizes, and evolving attributes remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies E = n × n for vectorization and clarifies matrix dimensions. The earlier appendix's optional diagonal-Hessian approximation suggestion is removed. Experimental budgets, processing instructions, and CPDstergm access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds recent network change-point work by Chen, Athreya, Zhang, and Kei and colleagues, references supporting separability, and background citations for latent-space models and Newton's method. These extend the literature discussion without substantially redefining the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method explanations receive localized rewriting. The notation subsection is removed, appendices are labelled A–E, and algorithmic guidelines move to Appendix D. The main six-section narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds consecutive-parameter difference annotations. Tables replace boxed grids with lighter rules, and Tables 1–6 add metric-direction arrows and bold best coverage values. Algorithm 1 is compacted and relocated, with other existing displays repositioned.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful conditional convergence and convexity justifications and makes the result tables easier to interpret. Proposition 1's exact-minimization assumption limits how directly it validates the finite-iteration implementation. These gains provide a modest net improvement despite the loss of some notation and optional Hessian-approximation guidance.
